exposure: Caesarean section in the second stage of labor
outcome: Maternal morbidities (extension of lower uterine segment incision, uterine atony, injury to urinary bladder, postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), sepsis, hospitalization for more than 5 days)
Neonatal morbidities (birth asphyxia, NICU admission, meconium aspiration syndrome, neonatal jaundice, neonatal sepsis)
cohort: The study included 90 women who delivered by caesarean section in the second stage of labor.
finding: The study found that caesarean sections during the second stage of labor are associated with a high likelihood of adverse maternal (PPH, sepsis, prolonged hospitalization) and neonatal (NICU admission, birth asphyxia, meconium aspiration syndrome) outcomes.
mod_finding: Caesarean section performed in the second stage of labor was associated with a high incidence of maternal morbidities (24.4% PPH, 15.6% sepsis) and neonatal morbidities (52.2% NICU admission, 29.8% birth asphyxia, 25.5% meconium aspiration syndrome).
